solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bell tower flowers enthralling relative (9)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: to enthral is to hold captive, so the flowers hold the relative inside them

blocks.note: two rivers, the CAM and the NILE: a river is something that flows

annotation.surface: A bell tower festooned with climbing flowers that have swallowed up a family member.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' is not blooms but things that flow: rivers, the crossword's favourite trick. The Cam runs through Cambridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A campanile is a free-standing bell tower, as beside many Italian churches.

entries.clue: Cave in wooded area sheltering everybody climbing (8)

indicatorNotes.sheltering: the wood shelters, so holds inside it, the next piece
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: a copse is a small wood

annotation.surface: Someone takes shelter in a cave in the woods while everyone climbs about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cave' pretends to be a noun, a place to shelter, but the definition is the verb phrase 'cave in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a roof or tunnel that caves in gives way and falls inward.

entries.clue: Masters chased by another reptile (5)

indicatorNotes.chased by: to be chased is to have something follow, so MBA comes after MA

blocks.note: MA, the initials of Master of Arts
another master's degree: Master of Business Administration

annotation.surface: A pair of masters being pursued across the grounds by a snake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' only makes sense once 'Masters' is read as a degree: the second is a different master's, the MBA.
annotation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast, venomous African snake.

entries.clue: Cycling sailor is (I reckon) very high (9)

indicatorNotes.Cycling: cycling moves the first letter round to the end

blocks.note: SALT (an old sailor) + IS gives SALTIS; its S cycles to the back

annotation.surface: A sailor on a bike, in the speaker's view, is flying very high.
annotation.walkthrough: The brackets make '(I reckon)' look like an aside; it is the textspeak IMO. A salt is an old hand at sea.
annotation.definitionFit: Altissimo is the musical term for the very highest register, above alto.

entries.clue: Rooms close to pipe under home become gas-filled (7)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, under places these pieces below the one they follow

blocks.note: a flat is a set of rooms

annotation.surface: Rooms near a pipe beneath the house start filling with gas: a plumbing emergency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near' but means the final letter. IN for at home is a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: To inflate, as a balloon does, is to swell as it fills with gas.

entries.clue: Delight papa lacking in taste (7)

indicatorNotes.lacking in: to lack something is to be without it, so the P goes

blocks.note: P = papa in the NATO alphabet
a penchant is a taste or liking; papa's letter is its first

annotation.surface: A father with no taste who is nonetheless a delight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lacking in taste' reads as a jibe at papa's style; in fact taste is PENCHANT, and papa is the letter it lacks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words once meant casting a spell, and now mean charming someone utterly.

entries.clue: Plunder smuggled in barrel firstly sent to port (5)

indicatorNotes.smuggled in: the answer is smuggled inside the words that follow
indicatorNotes.sent to port: port is the left, so in an across clue the letters travel right to left

blocks.note: barrEL FIRstly carries ELFIR across the word gap

annotation.surface: Contraband hidden in a barrel is shipped off to a harbour: smuggling in progress.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word sounds like smuggling at sea, but 'port' is the left-hand side, so the hidden letters are read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to plunder it, searching and stealing.

entries.clue: River fish, first to dive to the bottom, moved quickly (5)

indicators: first to dive to the bottom

indicatorNotes.first to dive to the bottom: the first letter sinks to the end, which is the bottom of a down entry

blocks.clueFragment: fish, first to dive to the bottom
blocks.note: DACE, a small river fish, with its D moved to the end

annotation.surface: A river fish plunges to the bottom and darts away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First to dive' reads as one fish diving before the others; it is the first letter of the fish doing the diving.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: racing is going at speed, so the past tense fits 'moved quickly'.

entries.clue: Person in lodge adapted for seamen (9)

indicatorNotes.adapted: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A lodge converted for use by sailors, with a person staying in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' pretends to be a cabin or guest house; it is a Masonic lodge, the meeting place of a branch of Freemasons.
annotation.definitionFit: Freemasons belong to local branches called lodges.

entries.clue: Creature highly exposed on burrow (6)

indicatorNotes.exposed: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

blocks.note: highly = VERY; stripped of its outer letters it leaves ER
a mine is a burrow dug into the ground

annotation.surface: A creature caught out in the open, perched above its burrow.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an animal out of its hole; the wordplay strips VERY bare instead.
annotation.definitionFit: The ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat.

entries.clue: Fruit cut with the other end (5)

indicatorNotes.cut: cut means shortened, so the fruit loses its last letter

blocks.note: 'the other' and 'it' are both euphemisms for sex

annotation.surface: A kitchen instruction: slice the fruit together with the other end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The other end' reads as the far end of the fruit; 'the other', a coy word for sex, is IT, and 'end' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a boundary is where a thing stops, the end of its reach.

entries.clue: Deal with press adopting electronic coverage for features? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.adopting: to adopt is to take in, so the press takes in the E

blocks.note: to face a problem is to deal with it
to cram is to press or stuff in

annotation.surface: A deal made with the newspapers to take up electronic reporting of their feature articles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press' and 'features' both sound like journalism; the features are those of the face, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Face cream is a layer spread over the face, so a covering for one's features.

entries.clue: Region stores ballast periodically dropped in huge lake (4,3)

indicatorNotes.stores: the region stores, so holds, the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.periodically dropped: every other letter is dropped, leaving the alternate ones

blocks.note: bAlLaSt with B, L, A and T dropped

annotation.surface: A region stocks ballast which is dropped at intervals into a vast lake, as from a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: Ballast dropped at sea is a real sailing picture, which hides that 'periodically dropped' is an instruction to lose alternate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, was once one of the world's largest lakes.

entries.clue: Muscle head attached to middle of ant’s hind-body (7)

indicatorNotes.attached to: the pieces are joined on one after another
indicatorNotes.middle of: the middle of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: abs are the stomach muscles; one is an AB
dome is slang for the head

annotation.surface: An insect anatomy lesson: which muscle attaches the head to the ant's rear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is so anatomical that 'head' looks like part of the ant; it is DOME, and ''s' stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An insect's abdomen is the rear section of its body, behind the thorax.

entries.clue: Romantic New Age books main inventory holds (14)

indicatorNotes.holds: the main holds, so contains, the pieces before it

blocks.note: the main is the open sea
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A romantic whose chief stock is New Age books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New Age' looks like a single phrase, but it splits into N and TIME. 'Main' is not 'chief' but the open sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A romantic, someone governed by feeling, is a sentimentalist.

entries.clue: Wheeling city gull catches wind like an owl? (9)

indicatorNotes.Wheeling: wheeling means turning round, so the letters are reversed
indicatorNotes.catches: the reversed letters catch, so hold, the next piece

blocks.note: to gull someone is to con them
to wind is to turn, as a key or a road does

annotation.surface: A gull wheeling over a city, snatched by a gust, is compared to an owl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gull' and 'wind' paint a seabird on the breeze; gull is the verb 'deceive', and wind rhymes with 'find', meaning to twist.
annotation.definitionFit: Owls are active at night, so nocturnal; the question mark marks the owl as only one example.

entries.clue: Rock setter’s stuffing in case 1 (9)

indicatorNotes.stuffing: the setter's letters are stuffed inside the next word

blocks.note: the setter is 'I am', so I'M

annotation.surface: A rock the setter has jammed inside a case, marked with the number 1.
annotation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across; it is simply ONE. 'Setter's' is 'setter is', so I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock, largely calcium carbonate.

entries.clue: Quote couple after site receives new order (8)

indicatorNotes.receives new order: the letters of site are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.after: couple comes after the rearranged site

annotation.surface: A builder's quote for a couple, given after the site takes a fresh order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quote' is the builder's price, not a line of text; 'couple' is a verb, to pair up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the trade sense: a builder's quote is a costed guess at the price.

entries.clue: Stresses about Omani MP changing sides? (14)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the stresses go round the next letters
indicatorNotes.changing: changing means the letters of OMANI MP are rearranged

annotation.surface: Political gossip: the pressures surrounding an Omani MP who is crossing the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing sides' reads as defecting, but 'changing' is the anagram and 'sides' is the definition, as in side dishes.
annotation.definitionFit: Accompaniments to a main dish are sides; the question mark flags the kitchen sense.

entries.clue: Upstart from Standard snubbed Evening Star (7)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: snub-nosed means short at the end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: par = the standard, as in golf
VENUS, the evening star, without its last letter

annotation.surface: London's Evening Standard snubbing the Evening Star newspaper as an upstart.
annotation.walkthrough: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper, so the surface reads as press rivalry; here Standard is PAR and the Evening Star is Venus.
annotation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a newcomer to wealth or rank, an upstart.

entries.clue: Grooms had food stored by partners (7)

indicatorNotes.stored by: the partners store the food, holding it between them

blocks.note: N and S are partners at bridge

annotation.surface: Bridegrooms whose meal was put aside by their partners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grooms' pictures bridegrooms beside their partners; it is the verb, tidies. North and South sit opposite as a pair at bridge.
annotation.definitionFit: To groom something is to neaten it.

entries.clue: Fiddle & Piano with one seafood option (6)

annotation.surface: A musical programme listing: fiddle and piano, plus a seafood dish.
annotation.walkthrough: Fiddle and Piano look like a duo of instruments; fiddle is the swindle, and piano the musical abbreviation P.
annotation.definitionFit: Scampi, breaded langoustine tails, is a standard seafood choice on a British menu.

entries.clue: Crowd turmoil with fellow knocked out by clubs (7)

indicatorNotes.knocked out by: the fellow is knocked out and clubs takes his place

blocks.note: a flutter is a state of agitation

annotation.surface: A crowd in turmoil as a man is clubbed unconscious.
annotation.walkthrough: The violence of 'knocked out by clubs' disguises a letter swap: C replaces F in FLUTTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: objects that clutter a room crowd it untidily.

entries.clue: Channel originally cancelled feature (5)

indicatorNotes.originally cancelled: the original, first letter is cancelled

blocks.note: a strait is a narrow sea channel; its original letter is the S

annotation.surface: A TV channel whose original feature programme was cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channel' and 'feature' sound like television; the channel is a strait of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trait is a distinguishing feature of character or looks.

entries.clue: Charlie once more forgetting name for weapon (7)

indicatorNotes.forgetting: to forget something is to leave it out, so the N goes

blocks.note: a charlie is a fool, an ass

annotation.surface: Charlie, once again forgetting someone's name, is told off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name or the NATO C; in British slang a charlie is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: An assagai, or assegai, is a slender spear used in southern Africa.

entries.clue: Transplant large number south of key (5)

indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, south of means below

blocks.note: a raft of things is a large number of them

annotation.surface: A plan to move a large population south of an island key.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a musical key, here G, not a low island.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from surgery and gardening: tissue or a shoot moved onto a new host.

entries.clue: Comic seen bending metal (9)

indicatorNotes.bending: bending twists the letters of seen into a new shape

annotation.surface: A comedian spotted performing a spoon-bending trick with metal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Comic' conjures a comedian doing a stage trick; it is a comic book, a manga.
annotation.definitionFit: Manganese is a hard, brittle metallic element.

entries.clue: Retired while visiting fine American city (5)

indicatorNotes.Retired: to retire is to go back, so the letters are reversed
indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor goes inside, so SA sits within the next pieces

annotation.surface: A retiree touring a pleasant American city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine American city' reads as one phrase, but the city is Japanese: 'American' just gives the final A.
annotation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan.

entries.clue: Passage from service after hollow invocation (5)

indicatorNotes.hollow: hollow means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters
indicatorNotes.after: the service comes after the emptied invocation

blocks.note: a let is a tennis serve that clips the net and is replayed

annotation.surface: A passage read in a church service after an insincere prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' and 'invocation' paint a church; the service is a tennis serve.
annotation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow passage of water running inland.

entries.clue: Draw articles on cover of Utopian novel (9)

indicatorNotes.cover of: the cover of a word is its outside, the first and last letters
indicatorNotes.on: the articles are placed on, so after, the other pieces

blocks.note: She, the novel by H. Rider Haggard

annotation.surface: Sketching some pieces for the jacket of a Utopian novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like sketching; it is drawing a sword. 'Utopian novel' seems one phrase, but the novel is Haggard's She.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to draw a sword is to pull it from its sheath.
